Yeb. 102ᵇ ממאי דהאי וחלצה … מִישְׁלַף הוא how do we know that this v’ḥal’tsah (Deut. XXV, 9) means taking off? Y. ib. XII, 13ᵃ top ושַׁלְפַת סיניה and she took off his shoe.
<cite ref="Shabbat 59b:16">Sabb. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>דילמא שָׁלְפָא וכ׳</he> she might take off (her jewelry) and show it.
Ib. מְשַׁלְּפָא (Pa.).
<cite ref="Shabbat 82a:13">Ib. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>ולא שליף ירקא וכ׳</he> and that no vegetable will be pulled, and eaten by you, out of the bunch &c.
<cite ref="Shevuot 31a:10">Shebu. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>שְׁלוֹפוּ</he>, v. <cite ref="Q00172"><he>פּוּזְמְקֵי</he></cite>.
Erub. 11ᵇ זיל שְׁלוֹף וכ׳ go and pull (the reeds) out, and throw them away; a. fr.—Trnsf. (cmp. נתר, שרי) to untie, annul.
<cite ref="Gittin 33b:3">Gitt. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>מילתא … למִישְׁלְפָהּ</he> an act performed in the presence of ten persons, requires ten for revoking it; a. e.—
<cite ref="Yevamot 109b:4">Yeb. 109ᵇ</cite> <he>ערבי שלציון דעבדי שְׁלוֹף דוץ</he> the guarantors of Shaltsiyon, where they practice ‘pull and stick in’, release the debtor and seize the guarantor.—
